newsitem.title: USA: Clinton reaffirms U.S support for Ireland talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton reaffirms U.S support for Ireland talks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton reaffirmed U.S. support for Northern Ireland peace talks on Wednesday, saying the multilateral negotiations had made "useful progress."

In a written statement issued as the U.S.-mediated talks went into recess until June 3 for British and local election campaigns, Clinton also pressed the Irish Republican Army to declare and implement an unequivocal ceasefire.
The IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein, has been barred from the talks until the IRA restores a ceasefire that it called in 1994 but broke last February.

Clinton said Washington strongly supported the talks in the belief that they offered "an unparalleled opportunity" for Northern Ireland political parties and the British and Irish governments to achieve a peace settlement.
Former Senator George Mitchell, a Maine Democrat and close friend of the president who was U.S. Senate majority leader from 1989 to 1994, chairs the negotiations.

"Under the skilled chairmanship of Senator George Mitchell and his colleagues, the talks have made useful progress. When the talks reconvene in June, it is important that they move quickly into substantive negotiations," Clinton said.
"I hope the participants will return to Stormont on June 3 determined to work creatively to make real progress. If they do, they will have my full support," he added.
